item.title: Trump's D.C. arch is now a military complex. Here's how that complicates things
item.description: The future of Trump's D.C. arch was already fraught. Then he rebranded it as a military complex. Experts say that only raises more legal and logistical questions.

item.title: A journalist once barred from the White House says this media ban is different
item.description: Jim Acosta has already been through a White House press-pass fight. Now, three news organizations are barred, and he says the press is showing solidarity that should have come sooner.

item.title: New DNA analysis adds evidence Jefferson fathered children with Sally Hemings
item.description: A lock of hair, 15 years of sleuthing and a 200-year-old question. In History by a Hair, Smithsonian Institution scholar Richard Kurin follows the DNA trail back to Thomas Jefferson.

item.title: How unarmed 911 teams are reshaping public safety in nearly 100 cities
item.description: Alternative response programs, where mental health clinicians respond to 911 calls instead of police, have proliferated since George Floyd's murder. What does it take to do this work well?

item.title: Grand jury finds no evidence of criminal conduct in the death of Nolan Wells
item.description: A grand jury found Wells' cause of death "consistent with drowning," and decided not to bring indictments. The teenager was found dead on Horn Island, after he boated there with friends to celebrate Independence Day.

item.title: What the equinox 'henge' effect tells us about U.S. cities
item.description: The fall equinox, which arrives Tuesday in the U.S., brings shorter days, and chances to witness alignment between Earth and the sun. It's a modern version of ancient observances of a celestial shift.

item.title: Aviation regulators turn to AI to help manage the nation's airspace
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration launched an ambitious $875 million push to make the U.S. airspace more efficient. But critics say it won't solve bigger problems with air traffic control.

item.title: The data center backlash is reshaping American politics — one community at a time
item.description: With striking speed, the widespread debate around data centers has become a fault line in American communities, cutting across political parties and forging unexpected alliances.
